sparse_layout: spatially spread 55-AP subset; not the exact AS coordinates
limits: Tests independent patch stacking at multiple sizes, not the private AutoStakkert algorithm.
Fixed 64-frame reference, 25476 screened frames, and 5738 contributions per AP.
120 circular APs at 65/93/131/185px, plus a spatially spread 55-AP subset count control.
The 55-AP subset does not reproduce the exact positions or size distribution in the AS screenshot.
Same original scalar quality weights and absolute frame brightness; no normalization or denoising.
Completed-patch registration adds another bilinear interpolation.
Frame-weight effective counts omit covariance effects from differing subpixel samples.
Fine-scale variation includes detail and artifacts; it is not a pure sensor-noise measurement.
The 65px controls are reconstructed from the preceding experiment and must match its floating images.
AS comparison uses the supplied manual-64 reference output, not a new AS run.

validation.focused_tests: 15 passed: 9 new multiscale controls plus 6 preceding patch controls
validation.single_scale_sharpening_controls: All six 65px outputs match the preceding experiment pixel-for-pixel.
validation.pilot_sampling_parity: 128-frame pilot: identical finite quality values and local shifts; identical reliability masks.
validation.visual_review: Inspected multiscale_local2_registered, multiscale55_local2_registered and scale185_local2_registered; no conspicuous patch-boundary seams, substantial grain remains.

conclusions: Independent multiscale patch stacking gives only a marginal further reduction beyond the previous best single-scale experiment.
The best combined-scale result is multiscale_local2_registered at 1.9606% and 1.8697% variation in the two disc regions.
This is a 2.07% and 0.96% reduction relative to scale65_local2_registered, and remains 3.42 and 2.91 times the supplied AS measurements.
The 55-AP count control is worse than the full layout and does not reproduce the AS result.
This controlled implementation does not support multiscale combination as the main explanation of the AS/PR gap; it does not establish the private AS implementation or identify sensor noise.
